question: Why are flooring quotes in Sarasota so different from each other?
title: Why Sarasota Flooring Quotes Vary So Much
h1: Why Are Flooring Quotes in Sarasota So Different From Each Other?
description: Sarasota flooring quotes can differ by thousands of dollars because contractors handle demo, leveling and moisture testing as separate line items, or don't.
capsule: Two Sarasota flooring quotes for the same room can differ by thousands of dollars because they scope different work under one number. One contractor's price might include demo, slab leveling and moisture testing; another's might cover material and labor only, with everything else billed later. The gap is almost always in what's included, not in the flooring product itself.

sections.h2: Why Do Two Quotes for the Same Room Look So Different?
sections.html:
Most of the time it isn't that one contractor is overcharging and the other is a bargain. It's that "install vinyl plank in the living room" means something different to each of them. A $3 per square foot quote and a $7 per square foot quote for the same 300 sq ft room might both be honest, if one is material and labor only and the other includes removing old carpet, leveling a low spot in the slab, and new baseboards.

We write every quote as separate lines, material, labor, removal, prep and trim, specifically so a homeowner can see where the number is coming from instead of trusting a single lump sum. That habit matters more here than in a lot of markets, because slab condition on the Gulf Coast varies house to house even on the same street, which means two quotes for neighboring homes can legitimately need different prep.

sections.h2: The Line Items That Actually Move the Price
sections.html:
A handful of items account for most of the swing between bids: what kind of demo is needed, whether leftover thinset has to be ground off a slab, whether a moisture test turns up a problem that needs mitigation, whether the floor needs self-leveling, and whether baseboards, transitions and furniture moving are included or billed separately. Scheduling assumptions can move a number too; a contractor who's padding in extra crew days for a tight timeline will price differently than one working a normal schedule. In a condo, acoustic underlayment required by the HOA is another line some contractors quote up front and others discover, and re-price, mid-job.

Self-leveling underlayment alone runs about $3-$9 per square foot professionally installed, and a standard 50 lb bag covers roughly 50 sq ft at a 1/8 in. pour or just 12-15 sq ft at 1/2 in., so a slab with a deeper low spot eats material fast. If a bid doesn't mention leveling at all, ask whether the contractor actually checked the floor or is assuming it's flat.

sections.h2: What 'Per Square Foot' Alone Doesn't Tell You
sections.html: A price per square foot without a product spec is close to meaningless. "$4 a square foot" could mean 12-mil vinyl plank on one bid and 20-mil SPC on another, or it could mean labor only with material bought separately. We quote by product tier for exactly this reason: a standard 12-mil vinyl plank job and a premium 22-mil SPC job aren't comparable even in the same room. The same problem shows up with tile: a $6 per square foot quote for standard 12 in. porcelain and a $6 per square foot quote for large-format 24 in. tile aren't really the same offer, since large-format tile typically needs more prep to install correctly.

sections.h2: How to Compare Two Bids Fairly
sections.html:
Ask each contractor for a written quote broken into material, labor, removal, prep and trim, and ask what happens if the slab moisture test comes back high, before you sign anything. If one quote is dramatically lower with no explanation, it's worth asking directly what's excluded rather than assuming it's the better deal. A five-minute conversation about scope usually surfaces the real difference faster than staring at two bottom-line numbers.

faqs.q: Is the cheapest flooring quote always the worst deal?
faqs.a: Not necessarily, but it's worth finding out why it's lower. Ask what's included in demo, prep and trim before assuming a low number is a bargain; sometimes it just means those costs get added later.

faqs.q: Should a quote include furniture moving?
faqs.a: It varies by contractor. Ask directly, since it's a common gap between a quote that looks cheap on paper and the final bill.

faqs.q: What should a written flooring quote include?
faqs.a: Material by product name and tier, labor, removal, any prep like leveling or moisture mitigation, and trim or transitions, each as its own line rather than one bundled total.
